newsitem.title: USA: St. Mary Land boosts reserves 58 pct.
newsitem.headline: St. Mary Land boosts reserves 58 pct.

text.p: St. Mary Land & Exploration Co said on Monday that it replaced 424 percent of its 1996 production, resulting in a 58 percent increase in proved reserves to 126.9 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 10.7 million barrels of oil.
The value of the reserves increased to almost $300 million as of December 31, 1996, St. Mary Land said.
Production in 1996 increased to an average of 10,315 barrels of oil equivalent per day, the company said.

St. Mary Land said the present value of estimated future net revenues before income taxes from the proved reserves increased 147 percent to $296.5 million as of December 31, 1996, compared with the end of 1995.
The value is based upon average prices of $25.08 per barrel of oil and $3.736 per million BTU of gas, the company said.
St. Mary Land, which expects its 1997 capital budget to be $65 million, said it expects finding costs to be $3.50 per barrel of oil equivalent for the year.
The company said the increased reserves came from investments in its core areas of Louisiana, southern Arkansas, and Eastern Texas.
